subject: Observability adaptor transport agreement — draft for review
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: acme-security@acmehealth.com, splunk-onboard@acmehealth.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Aug 2023 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability adaptor transport agreement — draft for review

Hi team,

Attaching a draft proposal for how Redwood will ship observability artifacts out of an on-prem / VPC deployment so they can be ingested by your Splunk instance without leaving your security perimeter. High level:

- Collector placement: a customer-managed collector (Filebeat + otel-collector) runs in the same subnet as the model runtime; it forwards logs to a short-lived mTLS proxy deployed in the customer VPC.
- Transport: proxy -> Splunk HEC over private peering. The proxy terminates client certs from the collector and authenticates to HEC using a scoped token; traffic is restricted to the Splunk private endpoint.
- AuthN / AuthZ: we propose issuing ephemeral certs from your enterprise CA (30m validity) via an automated CSR workflow; HEC tokens are rotated daily and stored in the onprem keystore.
- Evidence packaging: each export bundle includes an evidence_manifest.csv (schema v2 attached) that lists file hashes, timestamps, and sampling rate metadata for traces. Bundles are signed (GPG) and checksumed before delivery.
- Tracing hooks: OTLP traces are exported to an internal agent which redacts PII fields via a configurable mask rule, stamps trace.source=redwood, and forwards to the Trace ingress on the Splunk side. Sampling will default to 1% for production but can be increased for troubleshooting windows.

Open questions for ACME:
1) Do you require HSM-backed signing for the evidence manifests, or is KMS envelope encryption sufficient?
2) Are there IP allowlist constraints on egress proxies (we plan a private endpoint; we need the CIDR block list)?
3) For retention/archival, do you want a 90-day hot retention then 2-year cold archive, or something else?

Attachments: evidence_manifest.csv (template), schema_v2.yaml (fields + validation).

Please review and let us know if we should move this into an on-site proof-of-concept schedule. If this looks reasonable we'll propose a short ops-runbook and a two-week test window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior PM, Observability Integrations
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 9 Aug 2023 11:03:00 -0700

Quick read — looks good. A couple of asks from infra/security POV:

- Can we add an explicit KMS/HSM integration section for key rotation (we should show where customer-managed KMS is used vs Redwood-managed keys).
- For the ephemeral cert flow, add a recovery/fallback path if the CSR service is unreachable (e.g., short-lived token + cached cert policy).
- Include the expected log volume (GB/day) for the test so ACME can size the proxy and firewall rules.

I'll add inline comments to the Drive doc and propose wording for the keystore section.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Staff PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: acme-security@acmehealth.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, splunk-onboard@acmehealth.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Aug 2023 14:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Observability adaptor transport agreement — draft for review

Thanks for the detailed draft. A few items from our side before we greenlight a test:

1) Audit sample: send a sanitized sample of the on-prem audit log bundle showing timestamps, event ids, and the manifest.
2) Network policy: we require static allowlistable CIDRs for any proxy endpoints plus an egress-only network ACL. Can Redwood provide the exact CIDRs or a plan to publish them prior to the poke?
3) SOC2 evidence: we need a short write-up on how evidence manifests and bundle signing satisfy the collection and integrity controls in our audit.
4) Runbook: procurement needs a short runbook (2-3 pages) describing install, rollback, and certificate rotation in case operations needs to triage.

If these are OK we can schedule a short architecture review next week.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Security Architect
Acme Health - Security
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: acme-security@acmehealth.com, splunk-onboard@acmehealth.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Aug 2023 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability adaptor transport agreement — draft for review

Aisha — thanks, great questions. Short answers and attachments:

- Audit sample: attached sample_audit_log.txt (sanitized); also included a signed manifest showing hash entries.
- CIDRs: for the PoC we can provide a predictable /29 (documented in the attached runbook) and expand during production; long term we can support private peering and no public egress.
- SOC2 write-up: see section 2 of onprem_runbook.pdf — we map manifest signatures to control CC6.1 (integrity) and show rotation lifecycle.
- Runbook: attached onprem_runbook.pdf (2 pages) — covers install, canary, rollback, and CSR fallback.

Next step: propose a 30-min architecture sync on Mon 14 Aug at 10am ET to walk through the runbook and the sample logs. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Karthik
